title: Weak Pawns: Isolated, Doubled, Backward
description: Learn to recognize and exploit the three classic pawn weaknesses — and how to handle them when they are yours.

sections.title: The Isolated Queen Pawn
sections.content: An isolated pawn has no friendly pawns on adjacent files, so it cannot be defended by a pawn. It grants active piece play but becomes a target in the endgame. Blockade it with a knight and trade pieces to exploit it.

positions.commentary: Black has an isolated pawn on d5. White blockades it with a knight on d4 and aims to trade down to a winning endgame.
hints: A knight on d4 is ideal

sections.title: Doubled Pawns
sections.content: Doubled pawns cannot defend each other and often cannot advance. They can be useful when they open a file for a rook, but as a static weakness they are a long-term liability.

positions.commentary: White has doubled c-pawns. They are weak and can be fixed and attacked. Black will target them with pieces and the king.
hints: Try to free the doubled pawns

sections.title: The Backward Pawn
sections.content: A backward pawn lags behind its neighbors on a half-open file and cannot be supported by them. The square in front of it is a perfect outpost for the opponent. Pile pressure on it.

positions.commentary: Black's d6 pawn is backward on the half-open d-file. White stacks rooks on the d-file and wins it.

exercises.title: Blockade the Isolani
exercises.description: White to play. Establish the ideal blockade in front of the isolated d-pawn.
